key_insight: Increasing the barrel filling ratio from 43% to 53% makes detonation-sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings denser and more wear-resistant, even though friction increases slightly.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing barrel filling ratio is a practical process lever for improving the durability of thermal-spray protective coatings used in high-wear, severe-service components.
method: Detonation-sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings at 43% and 53% barrel filling ratios.
Compared microstructure and phase composition using microscopy and XRD.
Evaluated dry sliding wear with ball-on-disc tests at 10 and 15 N and 5 and 10 cm/s.
evidence_signal: The 53% coating showed a denser microstructure and achieved a minimum wear rate of 1.23 × 10^-4 mm3/(m·N) under tribological testing.
watch_item: Results are based on a narrow set of spray settings and dry-sliding conditions, so performance gains may not directly transfer to other loads, environments, or component geometries.
paper_title: Effect of Barrel Filling Ratio on the Microstructure, Phase Composition and Tribological Performance of Detonation-Sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr Coatings
